facts:
## CELL FACTS

Cell 木_偏财 (Wood carrying The Horizon). Persona The Horizon (偏财). Definition line: "Wide-ranging engagement, opportunity sensed at a distance". Keyword Reach, charge dynamic, poles catalyst Momentum / friction Scatter. Family function: Action. Cost dimension: opportunity sensed far off; the near things blur. Arena: horizon, wind, open road, far light, the next place. Classical portrait: wide-ranging engagement; opportunity sensed at a distance; windfall, generosity, the near things blur. Ruled domains: Opportunity, Ventures, Father. Sibling (other polarity of the family): 正财.
Element arena: Wood (trunk, branch, root, grain, growth, the forest). dm_element (which core reads this cell): Metal. structural_interaction seed: "Metal directing Wood broadly — precision ranging across living material".
- k2_overview: "Your Wood moves as the Horizon: growth that reaches for distant light. Opportunity, for you, is territory: new markets, new cities, branches extended where no one from home has grown. You expand naturally and prune reluctantly. Fortune arrives through the reaching. Roots decide how much of it you keep."
- k2_functional: "You grow toward opportunity steadily, extending reach every season without retreating."
- adj_chips: {"friction":["Scattered","Overgrown","Fickle"],"catalyst":"[REDACTED: the words under test]"}
- k2_domain_readings: {"Opportunity":"Opportunities appear to you as open land: markets unplanted, niches unclaimed. You see fertile ground others call wilderness. Scout it, but check the soil before transplanting everything.","Ventures":"Your ventures grow in groves: several trunks sharing a root system of skills and contacts. Let each mature before seeding the next. Orchards fail from planting fever, not planting.","Father":"The father-thread runs green and rangy: reach, enterprise, restlessness, wherever a paternal figure stood. Where that reaching shaped you, keep it. Where it left no roots, plant them yourself."}
- fn_reading.catalyst.ledger (three rows, index-aligned to adj_chips.catalyst; authored order is significance order):
  - row 0: [REDACTED: the target row]
  - row 1: [REDACTED: the target row]
  - row 2: [REDACTED: the target row]
- Sibling cell 木_正财 chips (nothing you write may fit the sibling): {"catalyst":["Cultivating","Compounding","Deep-rooted"],"friction":["Stuck","Plays it safe","Inflexible"]}
- Sibling cell 木_正财 catalyst row 0 drive passage, for the sibling test on the tension (this row must name a different either-or): "Improving what you already own comes easier to you than chasing what you don’t, and it shows everywhere you’ve settled. Care, in your hands, behaves like an investment: whatever you maintain appreciates, and whatever needs chasing, you mostly no longer bother to chase."

Core element Metal, energy element Wood. Law: Metal tames Wood (金克木: the knife prunes the branch). Relative to the core the energy is the tamed, so Wood is this core's Action. No chart is attached to this batch: the cell is written for every chart with a Metal core that shows Wood on the catalyst pole, so no percentage and no state of one chart appears in any value. The catalyst pole of Wood as the Action is the Overfueled band's case (the core has more than it channels); tone by pole: compliment. Rows: row 0, row 1, row 2, each with its three angles (drive, cost_self, cost_others: the drive, the cost to the reader, the cost to others; the app shows one angle per row by position rotation, so each passage must stand alone); one chip per row, written once and copied byte-identical onto the row's three fields. The pair cell 金_木's definition and advice for this pole are rewritten in the same batch (the pair skeleton) and are withheld here; no four-word run may be shared with them, so keep every phrase the ledger's own.

value.text: Spotting openings is what you do before anything is obvious. You carry less Wood than drive to spend, so you spot the far chance sooner than the one in your hand. Spot the near one as carefully, because it is yours to take.

value_b.text: You spot a chance early and trust the spotting. Wood is the energy you have least of, so you spot far things ahead of close ones. Spot one close thing a week with the same care, since the far one keeps.

value.text: Giving comes more easily to you than keeping, especially money. Being generous keeps the world feeling wide, so you give away a good month rather than save it. Keep giving, and hold one part back, because what you keep is what the giving stands on.

value_b.text: You give before you count, and rarely regret it. Holding back feels like holding your breath, so you give to whoever needs it ahead of your own plans. Give one month a plan as well, because a plan is how your generosity lasts.

value.text: Giving is your first answer to most things. Being generous feels more like you than being careful, so you give the extra ahead of putting any aside. Give yourself a part too, because the money you never keep is what giving costs you.

value.text: Whenever the people close to you run short, you give before being asked. Giving keeps you freer than being owed, so you give rather than build anything shared. Let them give back sometimes, since your giving takes from them the chance to be generous too.
